subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeretail.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models

Alex / Sam — thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points you described:
- Rising per-token costs across high-volume customer-facing flows (chat and summarization).
- Vendor lock-in concerns given product roadmap and desire for model experimentation.
- Compliance/data residency constraints for EU customers that limit forwarding data to third-party hosted inference.

Current stack:
- Production: OpenAI GPT-4.1 (primary) for chat + Anthropic Claude for higher-cost safety checks on select flows.
- Client-side orchestrator for prompt templates, simple caching in Redis, and limited batching today.
- Approx usage: ~60M tokens / month (peak ramp expected next quarter).

Success criteria for migration (what would make this project successful for Acme):
1) Equivalent or better user-facing quality on intent detection and summarization tasks (pass your internal eval suite).
2) Performance within 1.5x of current latency SLOs for 95th percentile in production (target <400ms p95 post-optimization).
3) Net unit cost reduction of >=30% at current scale (tokens served + infra).
4) Smooth rollout path with canary and fallback to existing APIs during the PoC window.

Compatibility needs we flagged:
- API parity for chat & streaming payloads (function/tool-calling patterns are used by your orchestrator).
- Model variants must support 8-bit/quantized weights for cost-sensitive paths.
- Deterministic prompt templating behavior and identical tokenization where possible (or a clear mapping plan).

Initial model shortlist we discussed:
- Llama 2 / 70B (quantized variants) — good balance of ecosystem support.
- Mistral Instruct / Mixtral — strong for instruction-following tasks.
- Falcon 40B — competitive latency on GPU; needs eval on summarization quality.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) Technical deep-dive w/ your infra + our SEs (Rishi) — target next week; goal: compatibility checklist and infra requirements.
2) 4-week PoC: dual-write traffic to Redwood private endpoint + canary against current vendor.
3) Evaluation: run your existing eval prompts + sample production traffic through A/B; report on quality/latency/cost.
4) If successful, scope Dedicated capacity and migration plan (SOW).

Attachments: I attached a short PoC proposal and a compatibility checklist we can use during the technical call.

Open questions (for you):
- Which two production flows do you want to prioritize for the PoC (we recommend chat support and order summarization)?
- Are there any regulatory constraints for token storage beyond EU residency?

Thanks — I’ll coordinate a time for the technical call once I hear which day next week works best.

Best,

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmeretail.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models

Thanks Marissa — this looks right to me. A few clarifications:
- Prioritize chat (customer support) and the weekly order summarization job for the PoC. Those have the clearest ROI.
- For compliance: we need EU data to remain in-region and an audit log of model access (who/when/prompt hash).
- We can commit engineering time (2 FTEs part-time) for the 4-week PoC window.

Rishi — can you propose 2-3 times for the deep-dive next week? Afternoon PST works best for us.

Alex
Head of AI Platform | Acme Retail
alex.johnson@acmeretail.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeretail.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models

Thanks Alex — afternoons PST work. Suggested slots: Wed 07/01 2:00pm PST, Thu 07/02 3:30pm PST, or Fri 07/03 1:00pm PST. I’ll prepare a compatibility checklist and a short runbook for the PoC (in particular: tokenization mapping, streaming API differences, KV cache migration strategy).

For the audit/logging ask: Redwood Private supports audit logs and we can surface prompt hashes rather than raw prompts if you prefer. We’ll note the EU-residency requirement in the PoC infra doc.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmeretail.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models

Great — locking in Wed 2026-07-01 14:00 PST for the technical deep-dive. Invites sent separately.

I attached the PoC SOW and the compatibility checklist we discussed; both are short and intended to make the first two weeks high-velocity. After the deep-dive Rishi will share the runbook and we’ll publish the test harness drive folder for your team.

Next steps for me:
- Send calendar invite (done)
- Share credentials and temporary Redwood Private endpoint for dual-write during PoC (after SOW accepted)
- Short intake form for engineering contact details and sample traffic (link in Drive).

Thanks again — excited to help you validate these models and reduce unit cost while keeping quality high.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
